Stefan Koellner, German country liaison officer, greet each other while exchanging the German flag and a patch after the first German Air Force F-35 aircraft lands at Ebbing Air National Guard Base, Arkansas, Oct. 6, 2026. The arrival marks the start of German F-35 pilot training at Ebbing ANGB, led by the 85th Fighter Group, a detachment of the 33rd Fighter Wing out of Eglin Air Force Base, Florida. The Foreign Military Sales program provides training to allied nations operating the F-35 to enhance interoperability, coalition capabilities, and global security partnerships. (U.S. Air National Guard photo by Tech. Sgt. Patricia Teare)
The collapse of Europe’s Franco-German-Spanish sixth-generation fighter program has left Germany searching for a new path, France possibly pursuing its own aircraft, and the UK-led Global Combat Air Programme (GCAP) as the continent’s only remaining multinational next-generation fighter effort. Meanwhile, the emergence of collaborative combat aircraft (CCA) is raising a fundamental question for European air forces: How much of their future combat capability needs to depend on traditional fighter jets?
The decisions come as European governments increase defense spending in response to Russian aggressiveness, reassess their dependence on American technology and support, and confront the cost of replacing aging aircraft. What emerges will determine not only the composition of Europe’s air fleets for decades, but also which countries control the technology, production, and sustainment of their combat aircraft.
In a four-part Breaking Defense video roundtable series on European airpower , Editor-in-Chief Aaron Mehta examined those issues with Douglas Barrie of the International Institute for Strategic Studies and Breaking Defense Europe Co-Editors Tim Martin and Elisabeth Gosselin-Malo. A separate conversation with Dave Alexander, president of General Atomics Aeronautical Systems, explored how industry is responding to Europe’s growing demand for unmanned capabilities.
Together, the discussions point toward a future combining upgraded fourth-generation fighters, F-35s, new sixth-generation aircraft, and a growing assortment of drones. The challenge is how European governments will afford, integrate, and sustain that mix while preserving sovereign control over critical military technologies.
Europe’s Existing Fighters Are Far From Over
Europe’s fighter-modernization challenge extends beyond developing sixth-generation aircraft. Governments must decide how much to invest in their existing fleets, what new capabilities are needed to counter emerging threats, and how to integrate crewed and unmanned systems into an airpower strategy that can meet both near-term operational demands and longer-term requirements.
“The Europeans are moving, if you like, from Rafael, Typhoon, Grippin, but at a pace where those aircraft are going to be in service well into the 2040s, possibly in some cases beyond,” said Barrie. “At the same time, obviously, the F-35 is appearing more and more in European air forces.”
Russia’s military threat is accelerating modernization across the continent, but national priorities differ. Countries bordering Russia such as the Baltic states are emphasizing smaller drones and expanding operator training across their armed forces. Larger European powers are investing in more sophisticated unmanned aircraft intended to operate alongside conventional fighters.
Lessons from Ukraine are also demonstrating the need to balance inexpensive first-person-view (FPV) drones with longer-range strike systems and traditional airpower. Gosselin-Malo emphasized the importance of “not putting all your eggs into one basket,” noting that FPV drones alone cannot deliver the range of capabilities required for modern warfare.
That mix is necessary as European governments seek to expand combat mass without relying entirely on additional crewed fighters. This also creates opportunities for domestic manufacturers to develop new aircraft and mission systems while established fighter programs continue production and modernization.
The Sixth-Generation Fighter Dilemma
The falling out among France, Germany, and Spain over the Future Combat Air System (FCAS) program has fundamentally changed Europe’s next-generation fighter landscape. Political disagreements and disputes over industrial responsibilities undermined the effort, leaving the UK/Italy/Japan GCAP program as the principal, remaining multinational sixth-generation fighter effort involving European countries. France is expected to pursue its own aircraft, while Germany must decide whether to join another partnership, pursue a national program, or redirect investment toward other capabilities.
GCAP is targeting 2035 for entry into service, a schedule driven largely by Japan’s need to replace its Mitsubishi F-2 fighters. There have been thoughts of adding partners to the program, though that would complicate negotiations over production, financing, and technology responsibilities, potentially delaying that timeline. Canada’s decision to become an observer in GCAP provides a way to evaluate the program without immediately entering those negotiations.
Even among the existing partners, industrial workshare remains unresolved. Martin reported that GCAP executives at the Farnborough Airshow acknowledged that “the workshare arrangements haven’t been agreed yet and that’ll come at the end of the concept phase.”
Similar hanging issues contributed to FCAS’s failure, although Barrie also pointed to the political structure underpinning the program. Changes in national leadership made it increasingly difficult to maintain agreement among participating governments and manufacturers. Germany now represents one of the most consequential uncertainties, given the financial resources it could bring to another fighter program.
“If you look at the sheer financial firepower Germany is bringing to defense right now, it is the kingmaker in a lot of ways,” said Mehta.
Airbus has signaled that any future arrangement must offer meaningful industrial participation. At the same time, additional F-35 purchases remain an option. Sweden’s Saab continues to deliver new JAS 39 Gripens while continuing exploratory research on its own next-generation fighter technologies.
The choices facing Germany and Sweden illustrate Europe’s longstanding difficulty reconciling national industrial priorities with the cost and complexity of developing advanced combat aircraft. Joining an existing program may reduce development costs, but also limits the influence a new participant can exert over its design and manufacturing responsibilities.
Members of the Air Force and Ohio Air National Guard look at laptops during field prototype testing evaluation for the Collaborative Combat Aircraft Portable Command and Control Enclave. (U.S. Air National Guard photo by Shane Hughes, 178th Wing).
Unmanned Aircraft Offer Another Path
Collaborative combat aircraft are emerging as another way for European air forces to increase combat capability without developing an entirely new crewed fighter. Designed to operate alongside manned platforms, CCAs could extend sensor coverage, carry weapons, support electronic warfare, and undertake missions that would permit crewed aircraft to operate at standoff distance.
CCAs, however, are substantially more complex and costly than the drones being used extensively in Ukraine. Barrie estimated that a CCA could cost about one-quarter of a crewed fighter, so equipping manned craft with multiple CCAs would represent a substantial additional investment.
Germany is aiming to field a CCA capability in 2029, potentially making it the first European country to operate such aircraft, according to Martin, while the UK has similarly committed funding for development. Still, Germany’s Luftwaffe leadership continues to emphasize the need for a sixth-generation crewed fighter, suggesting that unmanned aircraft will initially supplement rather than replace traditional combat aviation.
During the discussion, Mehta raised the possibility that Germany and other European countries could instead concentrate their resources on developing CCAs, continuing to operate existing fighters, and eventually acquiring a sixth-generation crewed aircraft developed elsewhere. That approach could offer an alternative to the industrial and political complications of another multinational fighter program, although it would require governments to reconsider the importance of independently developing a crewed combat aircraft.
This is where the case for sovereign control of mission software and electronic systems comes in. European operators of American aircraft including the F-35, however, may face restrictions on independently modifying certain capabilities, potentially slowing upgrades.
General Atomics Sees Industrial Sovereignty Driving Demand
The emphasis on national control is already influencing how American manufacturers approach Europe’s unmanned aircraft market. General Atomics has built a European presence through its MQ-9 family, extending that experience into development of CCAs and additional mission capabilities traditionally performed by crewed platforms. Industrial cooperation is central to that strategy, including European production of aircraft components, integration of locally developed sensors, and domestic maintenance and repair capability.
“You can go in there and have the best system in the world, but if you’re not willing to open up and make it theirs, make it their own, it’s not going to go anywhere,” said Alexander, emphasizing sustainment as an element of sovereignty. With aircraft potentially operating for 40 years, domestic maintenance and repair capabilities can be as important to a customer as participation in manufacturing, he noted.
General Atomics sees growing opportunities for its MQ-9B in maritime surveillance, anti-submarine warfare, and airborne early warning, where long endurance and lower operating costs could provide alternatives to larger crewed aircraft.
The same industrial approach is shaping its CCA offering, particularly as European requirements diverge from those driving US Air Force development.
“Most of the CCA customers are looking for air to ground, not air to air,” Alexander said, pointing to GA’s Gambit family of six variants built around capabilities such as ISR or strike that can integrate local payloads rather than depend entirely on US-developed mission equipment and software.
He emphasized that European countries could contribute their own artificial intelligence and autonomy capabilities, allowing them to adapt the platform to national requirements. That approach could also provide a path for European companies to participate in CCA development without building an entirely new aircraft, in the same way that the Netherlands has joined the US Air Force CCA program to provide wingmen for its Royal Netherlands Air Force F-35As.

BMW launches public charging promo for 2027 EVs
BMW’s electric vehicle lineup will look much different in 2027. The German luxury automaker is shaking things up with the arrival of its Neue Klasse EVs, bringing significantly longer ranges, faster charging times, and advanced new tech and features.
To sweeten the deal, BMW launched a new public charging promotion on Thursday for eligible model-year 2027 electric vehicles, including the new iX3, i5, and i7.
The new BMW ChargingNetwork package provides $500 in total credits. $300 of which includes a BMW ChargingNetwork credit that can be used at one of 15 public charging providers, such as ChargePoint, EVgo, Shell Recharge, and IONNA. The other $200 is for IONNA locations only.

On top of this, the promo includes a free one-year BMW Membership at IONNA. The membership provides a 25% discount on charging during the free year trial.
BMW iX3 50 xDrive (Source: BMW)
BMW said the charging credits will automatically apply after you enroll in the BMW ChargingNetwork.
You can enroll through the My BMW app. Under Charging, select Services, then Charging Wallet, and then BMW ChargingNetwork. Once complete, the credits and other benefits will show up in the Digital Charging Wallet and will be automatically applied to eligible charging sessions.
2027 BMW iX3 interior (Source: BMW)
Which one to choose? The 2027 iX3 is BMW’s first Neue Klasse vehicle. Based on its sixth-generation (Gen6) eDrive, the iX3 delivers an EPA-estimated range of up to 434 miles.
Inside, it features BMW’s revamped Neue Klasse interior design. The setup includes the new BMW Panoramic Vision, a full-length display spanning the base of the windshield, and a large 17.9″ infotainment screen running the latest BMW Operating System X.
The 2027 i7 also incorporates elements and tech from BMW’s Neue Klasse platform, with up to 362 miles of range.
The i7’s interior also gets the BMW Panoramic Vision display, a 17.9″ infotainment screen, and a standard 14.6″ passenger screen. For the rear passengers, BMW’s flagship sedan includes a 31.3″ 8K theater screen that folds down from the ceiling.
Meanwhile, the 2027 i5, which still offers up to 310 miles of range, is not built on the dedicated Neue Klasse platform.
As part of a mid-cycle refresh, it adopts BMW’s new style but lacks some Neue Klasse tech and features found on the iX3 and i7.
In the first quarter of 2027, BMW will launch the new iX5 and i3. Both are based on the Neue Klasse platform.

This Ember RV Travel Trailer Can Turn Its Bunk Room Into a Mobile Office or Cargo Space
16 photos
Photo: Ember RV/ That RV Girl
No two RV trips are the same, and that is why flexibility is an important aspect when choosing a travel trailer. One weekend might be about family time, the next could be about outdoor adventures, while another might call for a designated workspace on the road. A travel trailer with a fixed floor plan might feel too rigid when your adventure needs change.
That’s why travelers are now looking for RVs that can adapt to their traveling plans. Ember RV understands this need for increased flexibility on the road and has introduced a new travel trailer that can do more than one thing. Meet the Touring Edition 2850DBL, a travel trailer that integrates the manufacturer’s exclusive EmberTrack E-track system that has versatility written all over it.
The EmberTrack E-track is a really interesting configurable setup that allows owners to transform the rear section of the RV into whatever you need, from storage space to bunk room, workspace, or an open cargo area. This versatility lets you transform the unit from a couple’s travel trailer to one suitable for family camping or for working on the road.
Ember RV’s Touring Edition is a premium travel trailer lineup aimed at RVers who want an elevated camping experience, with more comfort, durable construction, refined finishes, and confident towing for anything from weekend adventures to longer trips.
Photo: Ember RV/ That RV Girl The new 2850DBL is a two-axle model with one slide-out and a rare two-door floor plan. The main entry door opens into the living area, while the secondary one enters the private front master suite. The towable RV measures 32 feet and 11 inches (10 meters) in overall length, but it feels more spacious than its footprint thanks to that slide-out and its 8-foot (2.4-meter) width.
Like all the models in the Touring Edition lineup, this model is built with laminated aluminum-framed construction, Azdel Onboard composite exterior walls with gel-coated fiberglass finish, and a fully walkable roof covered in one-piece Tufflex PVC roofing. It rides on aluminum rims with Goodyear Endurance tires and a CURT Touring Coil Suspension system with heavy-duty coil springs and shock absorbers on each wheel, which is meant to make towing smoother.
The 2850DBL is one of those RVs that provide residential comfort inside but also encourage outdoor living . It features a 20-foot (6-meter) power awning that creates a large shaded area beside the trailer. Underneath, there is a clever fold-up “Bar-V” window and a fold-down table, creating a connection between the interior living area and the outside campsite. It can also be closed off with an integrated screen or shade.
Photo: Ember RV/ That RV Girl The exterior station includes a TV, a bar section, standard outlets, and plenty of space to put an induction stove for cooking if needed, creating a great setup for outdoor cooking, camp-day cocktails, tailgating or watching a game outside.
However, the feature that really sets this model apart is the EmberTrack E-track system at the rear. Another fold-up window and fold-down bartop open to reveal a generous open space that can be configured as you please. From the factory, this space comes equipped with two double-over-double bunk beds, but these aren’t permanent installations. They’re mounted on E-track rails, allowing for plenty of flexibility .
Photo: Ember RV/ That RV Girl Owners can opt for a single-over-double arrangement or individual single bunks, or position the bed bases so that they can create shelves or a desktop, turning this rear area into a mobile workspace. The beds can also be mounted on an upper position or removed altogether to free up cargo space for hauling e-bikes, dog kennels, outdoor gear, and more. You can even hang a hammock in this space and chill out while enjoying the breeze. A large baggage door at the rear makes getting larger things inside easier.
Other exterior features include a pass-through storage compartment at the front and a tongue gear box with two compartments - one for two propane bottles and one for tools.
As for the interior arrangement, the 2850DBL floor plan comprises a private front bedroom, a central living and cooking area, plus a bathroom and the repositionable EmberTrack bunk/storage system at the rear.
Photo: Ember RV/ That RV Girl The slide-out adds extra width to the living area and houses theater seating with three recliners and rotating side tables, a 12-cubic-foot 12V French-door refrigerator, and a floor-to-ceiling pantry. Across the living area, there is what the manufacturer calls the “EmberFlex Dinesk,” a long bar table that can be configured as a dining table, a bar, or a desktop, depending on what you actually need. It connects to the outdoor fold-down bartop and a dining table slides from underneath it when you need space for more people to sit down and enjoy a meal together.
The kitchen comes with solid-surface countertops, base and upper cabinets, an undermount stainless steel sink, and a flip-up counter extension. The appliance package includes the aforementioned fridge, a cast-iron three-burner cooktop, and an over-the-range convection microwave/air fryer. There is also a coffee bar next to the sofa, with a small counter space and storage.
Photo: Ember RV/ That RV Girl The front bedroom is fully enclosed and fitted with a walk-around residential queen bed measuring 60 by 80 inches (152 by 203 cm). The bed has integrated storage underneath, but it’s also flanked by two wardrobes. Practical nightstand cubbies with outlets are integrated on either side of the bed, and there is also TV prep on the opposite wall. Apart from the “real queen” bed, the nicest feature is that the bedroom has its own entry door for direct access from the outside.
The bathroom inside this RV is compact but so well designed that it feels residential. It includes a large shower with sliding door, a nice size vanity, a corner medicine cabinet, a toilet, and even additional storage cubbies.
Ember RV has also equipped this new travel trailer with the systems needed for extended off-grid adventures. The mandatory Off-Grid Solar Package gives you 400 watts of rooftop solar panels, a 2,000-watt inverter, and a Victron MPPT solar controller. The 2850DBL also carries 55 gallons (208 liters) of freshwater, while the gray and black water tanks hold 70 and 35 gallons (265 and 132 liters), respectively.
Other standard features include a HD television, two Furrion Chill Cube AC units with heat pumps, the EmberLink smart RV system, a 12V Multi-speed Fan, and a 30K BTU furnace.
The Ember RV Touring Edition 2850DBL has a dry weight of 7,395 pounds (3,354 kg), a gross vehicle weight of 9,495 pounds (4,306 kg), which leaves it with a cargo carrying capacity of 2,100 pounds (952 kg). Pricing for this travel trailer starts at $78,355.

Posted By: Colin McClelland November 6, 2026
India is subsidizing battery storage and lithium and nickel processing to build a domestic supply chain, but securing raw materials and competing with established overseas processors remain obstacles.
The cabinet approved 145 billion rupees (US$1.5 billion) for grid-scale storage Wednesday, alongside 28.14 billion rupees for lithium and nickel processing. The measures support both demand for battery materials and the plants that would supply them.
“Midstream bottlenecks like feedstock uncertainty, price volatility, and global overcapacity are discouraging investment in refining and processing,” Kaira Rakheja, an energy analyst at the Institute for Energy Economics and Financial Analysis, said in a May assessment of India’s minerals strategy.
While the new support addresses a financing gap identified by researchers, building processing capacity doesn’t secure the minerals to feed it. For mining companies, India could become another customer outside China; turning that opportunity into investment will require supply agreements that work for both Indian processors and overseas producers.
Storage program
The storage program targets 92 gigawatt-hours of capacity through fiscal 2030–31, including 30 GWh of batteries with a minimum 40% domestic-content requirement. It also supports 60 GWh of pumped hydro and 2 GWh of alternative storage technologies, the government said.
The benefits for miners will depend on the technology deployed. Pumped hydro accounts for most of the supported capacity, while lithium iron phosphate batteries dominate battery storage without requiring nickel or cobalt in their cathodes. The International Energy Agency puts their share of battery energy storage systems above 90%.
Public and private electricity distributors will be eligible for support for battery and pumped-hydro projects, with capacity awarded through competitive tariff bidding. Storage would help shift surplus renewable electricity into periods of higher demand.
Under the separate processing program , subsidies will cover 30% of eligible investment in four plants over five years. Two lithium plants must each have capacity of at least 30,000 tonnes, while two nickel plants must each have at least 50,000 tonnes.
The announcement did not specify whether those tonnages refer to feedstock, finished compounds or contained metal, or the period over which capacity is measured.
The program targets the conversion of ores and intermediate products into high-purity compounds, with cobalt potentially recovered as a nickel by-product. Applicants must first meet technical requirements, after which the government will select bidders seeking the least capital support, it said.
The cabinet announcement didn’t name beneficiaries or identify their feedstock suppliers.
Foreign input
India’s processing ambitions depend on securing foreign minerals, technology and financing, limiting what domestic subsidies alone can achieve, Zainab Usman and Vivek Shastry argued in an Oct. 28 analysis published by Columbia University’s Center on Global Energy Policy.
But that strategy faces competing industrial ambitions. Resource-rich countries increasingly want to process their own minerals, while wealthier partners seeking diversified supplies also want to retain manufacturing, the researchers said.
India’s measures follow its critical minerals agreement with the United States in May, which established a framework for cooperation on mining, processing and supply security.
The financing problem extends beyond construction costs. In their May assessment , researchers at the Institute for Energy Economics and Financial Analysis and Climate and Sustainability Initiative identified volatile prices, long project timelines and uncertain returns as obstacles to private investment. They also called for closer links between mineral processing and manufacturing incentives.
Usman and Shastry identified joint ventures, long-term offtake agreements, technology partnerships and selective co-investment as ways for India to build relationships that benefit both suppliers and customers.

source_document.body:
Copper wire at a Freeport-McMoRan facility. Credit: Freeport-McMoRan via Facebook.
By: Northern Miner Staff November 6, 2026
Copper could fall further as Democratic Party gains in the United States midterm elections weaken expectations for import tariffs and raise doubts about projected demand from data centres, TD Securities says.
Three-month copper futures on the London Metal Exchange declined to about $13,779 per tonne, or $6.25 per lb., by late afternoon Friday in London, their lowest level since July, data show. The metal has retreated from September’s intraday peak of almost $6.80 per lb. as traders reassess demand and the incentive to accumulate U.S. stockpiles.
“We continue to expect the red metal to face further downside from here,” TD Securities managing director and global head of commodity strategy Bart Melek said in a note published Thursday.
The risk is that copper loses some of the support from U.S. stockpiling before expected growth in data-centre consumption materializes. Mine disruptions and tight supplies outside the U.S. could nevertheless limit the decline, Fitch Group’s BMI research and data unit says.
Stockpiling risk
Democratic gains could increase resistance to power-hungry data centres, a source of expected copper demand growth, TD says. Affordability concerns ahead of the 2028 presidential vote could also reduce the appetite for aggressive copper tariffs, it says.
“With many states slated for significant AI data center development turning blue, and opposition to new construction potentially growing, AI-driven copper demand could fall meaningfully short of current projections,” Melek wrote. “At the same time, many traders believe aggressive copper tariffs are now less likely with the Democratic Party controlling the U.S. Congress, and affordability the Achilles’ heel for the governing party heading into 2028.”
U.S. copper inventories total about 1.6 million tonnes, TD estimates. Reduced stockpiling incentives and the disappearance of profitable price differences between American and overseas markets could halt additional inflows for a significant period. Slower imports would not necessarily mean an equivalent decline in industrial consumption.
“As such, another $500 per tonne drift lower would not be a major surprise,” Melek wrote. Based on Thursday’s closing copper price of $13,843 per tonne in London, that would represent a drop of about 3.6%.
BMI also sees tariff policy as the immediate catalyst, although it expects mine constraints and electrification demand to cushion any correction. It expects copper to average $13,500 per tonne this year and $12,900 in 2027.
“U.S. tariff uncertainty remains the clearest near-term catalyst for copper, in our view,” BMI said in a report published Thursday.
Possible duties
Washington’s July 2025 copper proclamation outlined possible refined copper duties of 15% from January 2027, rising to 30% in 2028, subject to a subsequent presidential determination. While Democratic gains could increase political pressure over the decision, the proclamation leaves it with the president — and the proposed levies remain unenacted. Separate 50% duties on certain semi-finished copper products and copper-intensive derivative products took effect in August 2025.
Anticipation has nevertheless redirected trade. Higher Comex prices relative to London encouraged shipments into American warehouses before potential tariffs, reducing metal available elsewhere. Comex inventories rose about 62% from January through Wednesday, BMI reported, with those warehouses holding about 70% of global exchange copper stocks on Oct. 30.
The dislocation overlays a concentrated supply chain. Chile supplied 68% of U.S. refined copper imports during 2021–24, followed by Canada at 16%, U.S. Geological Survey data show. China produced an estimated 14 million tonnes of refined copper in 2025, nearly half the global total.
Metal scramble
Chinese buyers are paying more to secure immediately available metal. The Yangshan import premium exceeded $200 a tonne on Wednesday, its highest since records began in 2017, BMI reported. Yet Melek argues that even China’s scramble for supplies has proved insufficient to prevent prices slipping below $14,000.
A tariff retreat would probably slow American imports before prompting substantial re-exports, BMI says, because shipping metal back overseas requires prices to cover freight and handling.
Supply remains a counterweight. BMI cut its 2026 mine production growth forecast to 1.1% from 2.4%, citing Chilean weakness and constraints at Freeport-McMoRan’s (NYSE: FCX) Grasberg operation in Indonesia and Ivanhoe Mines’ (TSX: IVN; US-OTC: IVPAF) Kamoa-Kakula complex in the Democratic Republic of Congo.

MP Materials' Mountain Pass rare earths mine in southern California is the only rare earths producer in the United States. Credit: MP Materials
Posted By: Henry Lazenby November 6, 2026
MP Materials (NYSE: MP), America’s only rare earth miner, earned an unexpected adjusted quarterly profit as sales volumes of magnet-making rare earths nearly doubled and a specialty-material shipment boosted revenue.
MP posted an adjusted $8.8 million (C$12.3 million), or 4¢ a share, in the three months to Sept. 30, the company reported Thursday. The result, which excludes expenses including stock-based pay and plant startup costs, beat analysts’ forecast of a 1¢ loss and reversed a 10¢ loss a year earlier.
“Our growth is supported by contracted cash flows, committed customers and long-term partnerships across industry and government,” CEO James Litinsky told analysts on Thursday’s earnings call.
The performance by the company, which mines and processes rare earths at Mountain Pass in California, about 80 km southwest of Las Vegas by road, highlights the growing contribution from a rare earth processing business. MP is building a domestic magnet supply chain with direct U.S. government equity investment. Sustaining that improvement will matter while finished-magnet sales build gradually.
Shares rose 4.5% to $35.25 around mid-Friday in New York, valuing the Las Vegas-based company at about $6.3 billion.
Sales jump
Revenue nearly tripled to $147.7 million, about 27% above the Zacks Investment Research consensus estimate. Adjusted earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization (EBITDA) reached $41.1 million, reversing a $12.6-million loss a year earlier.
However, revenue included a $31.6-million sale of mixed rare earth material from inventory to a U.S. aerospace and defence customer. Chief financial officer Ryan Corbett described the transaction as a one-time sale. Excluding it, revenue would have been about $116.1 million, close to analysts’ expectations.
MP still recorded a net loss under standard accounting of $20.7 million, or 12¢ a share, compared with $41.8 million, or 24¢, a year earlier.
Price support
The company separately recognized $8.1 million in income under its Pentagon price-protection agreement. The 2025 partnership established a 10-year floor of $110 per kg for neodymium-praseodymium, used in powerful permanent magnets, alongside financing and commitments to buy future magnet output.
Sales of neodymium-praseodymium rose 94% to 1,020 tonnes, while production increased 41% to a quarterly record of 1,018 tonnes.
For the fourth quarter, management expects sales of about 1,000 tonnes at a realized price of roughly $100 per kilogram. It expects another $8 per kg in price-protection income on those sales.
Magnet ramp
MP completed magnet qualification with General Motors (NYSE: GM), clearing the way for saleable deliveries and revenue this quarter from its Independence plant in Fort Worth, Texas.
Corbett cautioned that shipments would build slowly as GM uses existing supplies and introduces MP’s magnets into individual vehicle programs and plants. The segment is expected to generate only modest adjusted EBITDA in 2027, before showing its full earnings power in 2028.
The company’s larger 10X magnet plant in Northlake, Texas, remains scheduled to begin commissioning in late 2028.

President Santiago Peña in his televised resignation speech. ( Screenshot from France24 | YouTube. )
Posted By: Cecilia Jamasmie November 6, 2026
Paraguay’s President Santiago Peña faced continuing impeachment proceedings Friday after submitting his resignation amid a banking crisis, weeks after Uranium Energy (NYSE-A: UEC) announced plans to invest $12 million (C$17 million) in the country’s uranium sector.
Peña offered to resign Thursday following the collapse of Ueno Bank, with which he had business ties. Congress had not accepted his resignation, leaving him formally in office as the Senate considered his removal .
The turmoil follows an October visit by U.S. Deputy Secretary of State Christopher Landau that brought investment announcements and plans for closer nuclear cooperation. UEC’s proposed spending would develop one of its Paraguayan uranium concessions, according to a government account of the visit.
The developments put Paraguay’s political crisis alongside an effort to attract American capital into its small mining sector. The country has identified uranium and titanium resources, but turning those deposits into operating mines will require further investment and development work.
Uranium Energy shares traded 4.6% stronger at $6.78 Friday morning in New York after falling nearly 10% the day before. The company’s market capitalization is about $3.4 billion. The stock has traded between $6.12 and $20.34 over the past year.
US minerals push
Paraguay and the United States signed a critical minerals memorandum of understanding earlier this year, followed by a separate nuclear cooperation memorandum on Aug. 4.
During Landau’s October visit, the countries announced negotiations on a so-called Section 123 agreement. Once in force, that agreement would establish the legal framework for major U.S. civilian nuclear equipment and material exports to Paraguay.
UEC’s Paraguayan portfolio includes the Yuty and Oviedo uranium projects and the wholly owned Alto Paraná titanium project, about 100 km north of Ciudad del Este.
Alto Paraná has indicated resources of 70 million tonnes grading 7.6% titanium dioxide and inferred resources of 3.58 billion tonnes grading 7.31% titanium dioxide, according to the company’s technical disclosures.
A November 2023 initial assessment , prepared under US S-K 1300 disclosure standards, estimated a base-case after-tax net present value of $419 million at an 8% discount rate and an internal rate of return of 21%.
The base case contemplated annual production of about 150,000 tonnes of high-titanium slag and 100,000 tonnes of high-purity pig iron. The preliminary assessment incorporates indicated and inferred resources; it does not establish mineral reserves.
Investment hurdles

He also identified gaps in geological information, saying only about 4% of Paraguay had been mapped at a scale of 1:100,000. Better mapping and an effective geological survey would help companies assess exploration opportunities, he said.
UEC identifies access to hydroelectric power and river transport through neighbouring countries as advantages for its Paraguayan assets. Whether the political turmoil changes the company’s development plans remains a question requiring a direct company response.

1966 Shelby GT350 Is a Rare Survivor, Owner Turned Down $250K at Mecum, New Price Is 20 Times Less
36 photos
Photo: Mecum
Shelby Mustangs aren’t the cars to make gearheads look elsewhere. Their asking prices, on the other hand, could make even the strongest cardiac muscle lose its tempo, and temporarily disconnect brain from mouth, leading to a spontaneous eruption of vocal impressions about the situation. After all, a quarter million dollars isn’t exactly lunch money for anyone, be them at whichever end of a sale. And yet, one owner of a specific ’66 GT350 thought again of just such an offer. And denied it.
When a quarter-million-dollar offer fails to secure a 60-year-old Ford Mustang, casual observers might assume the seller had an argument with reality, and sent it to sleep on the couch for a while. On October 24, 2026, at the Mecum Dallas/Fort Worth auction in Texas, bidding on a 1966 Shelby GT350 Fastback stalled at $250,000. The vlogger from the CARFINDER YouTube channel (who is a retired used car dealer) provides a walkaround of the rare fastback which came out from under the gavel unsold.
Bearing Shelby serial number SFM6S2178, this car was the 2,178th example built for the 1966 model year, and is titled as a 1966 Ford. Its odometer displays 47,506 miles, or 76,454 kilometers, a figure that could partially justify the high reserve set by the seller. However, it’s not an unmolested survivor – it wears an older repaint in the original Ivy Green metallic livery, complemented by white racing stripes.
Under the fiberglass hood reinforced by a steel frame sits the matching-numbers K-code HiPo 289 V8, Ford’s trusty Hi-Power 4.7-liter small-block from the mid-sixties. Dressed with hollow-letter Cobra finned aluminum valve covers and an aluminum high-rise intake manifold topped by a 715-cubic-feet-per-minute Holley four-barrel carburetor, the solid-lifter powerplant delivers 306 horsepower, or 310 metric horsepower, at 6,000 rpm, and 329 lb-ft (446 Nm) of torque at 4,200 revs.
Power reaches the rear axle through a close-ratio 4-speed manual Borg-Warner T-10 gearbox. The mechanical package of SFM6S2178 also includes front disc brakes, under-ride traction bars, functional rear brake cooling scoops, and 14-inch GT6 Shelby 10-spoke alloy wheels. Inside, the black vinyl cabin retains its factory back seat delete package shelf, radio delete plate, wood-rimmed steering wheel, and dash-mounted tachometer.
As the CARFINDER host observed in Fort Worth, the aged cabin and engine bay reflect the authentic, unrestored survivor theme.
Understanding why $250,000 could not buy this Ivy Green survivor requires examining the origins of the GT350 nameplate. In 1964, Ford division chief Lee Iacocca recruited Le Mans winner Carroll Shelby to turn the new Mustang into an SCCA B-Production road racer capable of defeating Chevrolet Corvettes. When Shelby asked engineer Phil Remington how far the main office stood from the Venice fabrication shop, Remington estimated 350 feet.
Photo: Mecum That casual measurement inspired the GT350 moniker, which originally spanned six model years from 1965 to 1970 with 7,053 classic examples built before returning for 325 post-title conversions between 2011 and 2014 and 24,211 factory cars from 2015 to 2020. Launched on January 27, 1965, the inaugural 1965 model saw 562 fastbacks assembled, comprising 521 street cars, 34 GT350R race cars, a couple of R-model prototypes, four drag cars, and a street prototype .
Every 1965 Shelby GT350 was a Wimbledon White fastback powered by the 289 Hi-Po V8 through a 4-speed manual transmission. For 1966, Shelby broadened its appeal across 2,378 units (1,365 street fastbacks, 999 Hertz rental fastbacks, the GT350Hs, a pair of Hertz prototypes, four factory drag cars, one Paxton-supercharged prototype, and four special-order convertibles.
While retaining the 306-horsepower, 289-cubic-inch V8 and standard 4-speed manual gearbox, the 1966 lineup introduced a 3-speed Ford C4 automatic transmission, optional rear seats, plexiglass quarter windows, and new colors like Ivy Green. In 1967, Shelby built 1,175 restyled GT350 fastbacks—plus 26 Group II notchback racers—retaining the 289-cubic-inch V8 with 4-speed manual or 3-speed automatic transmissions.
Photo: Mecum For 1968, production shifted to Michigan, yielding 1,657 cars split between 1,253 fastbacks and 404 convertibles. Those 1968 models, including 224 Hertz fastbacks, replaced the K-code engine with a 302-cubic-inch, (4.9-liter) V8 rated at 250 horsepower (253 PS), paired with 4-speed manual or 3-speed automatic transmissions.
In 1969, Ford built 960 GT350s—821 SportsRoof fastbacks, including 151 Hertz units, and 139 convertibles—before re-vinning 318 leftover cars—261 fastbacks and 57 convertibles—as 1970 models, all using a 290-horsepower, 351-cubic-inch (5.8-liter) Windsor V8. Transmissions were unchanged: 4-speed row-your-owns or 3-speed automatic.
Decades later, Shelby American revived the badge from 2011 to 2014 on 325 post-title fastbacks and convertibles using the first-gen 5.0-liter Coyote V8 engines with 6-speed manual or automatic transmissions. Ford then produced 24,211 factory fastback coupes from 2015 to 2020 (137 in 2015, 6,169 in 2016, 7,115 in 2017, 4,378 in 2018, 3,595 in 2019, and 2,817 in 2020) equipped with a 526-horsepower 5.2-liter flat-plane-crank V8 and 6-speed manual transmission.
Photo: Mecum The current S650 Mustang brough about the fourth iteration of the fabled Shelby GT350 nameplate, again as a post-title-only machine based on the Mustang GT and its 480-hp Coyote V8 (Generation 4).
Recent auction metrics explain why the consignor of SFM6S2178 rejected $250,000 in Texas. Across 342 verified classic Shelby GT350 sales recorded over the past 5-year period by classic.com , the overall median sale price across all 1965 to 1970 model years sits at $151,200.
Over the past twelve-month period, 26 classic GT350s changed hands between $81,400 and $1,100,000, yielding a Year-To-Date median of $218,500 across all vintage years and a $310,700 average specifically for 1966 models. And that’s before factoring in the color: Ivy Green was not a commonly ordered shade on ’66 GT350s. Factory records didn’t specify the production by paint choice, but over the years, enthusiasts have compiled a database showing how scarce this specific shade is.
Photo: Mecum Of the 999 Hertz cars, just 59 came in Ivy Green; the Paxton supercharged prototype was also colored like them. The Shelby American Automobile Club estimates under 15% of production cars have been splashed Ivy Green from the factory, meaning only about 200 examples were made like the one in the gallery.
Rare, but what’s the correct price for that lack of commonality? Let me know in the comments if you have an idea. Just so you know, it’s on the market again, and the current bid is a microscopic $11k, with two more days to go. However, the Buy It Now price is $12,500, exactly 20 times under the high bid from October 24. There's also a $11,200 Facebook Marketplace listing for it (in Anchorage, Alaska), but the seller's profile would have one think the ad is a scam.

Toyota China Recalls Land Cruiser Prado Hybrid and Lexus GX 550h for Potential Fuel Leak
49 photos
Photo: Toyota
Per the State Administration for Market Regulation, the world's largest automaker has to fix a bunch of body-on-frame sport utility vehicles in China. This recall affects 47,347 hybrid units of the domestically produced Prado (a.k.a. Land Cruiser in the United States or 250 series if you're into Land Cruisers) and 8,130 imported examples of the mechanically similar Lexus GX 550h.
As it happens, the problem with these body-on-frame SUVs can be found where customers rarely look. The retainer inside the fuel link quick connector may lift due to unexpected external forces, and in extreme cases, detachment could occur. This, in turn, creates the possibility of a catastrophic fuel leak.
Toyota's Chinese subsidiary has not specified which road conditions or driving maneuvers trigger the problem. The filing published by the SAMR only describes the circumstances in general, and that would be that, unfortunately. FAW Toyota Motor is the legal entity behind recall S2026M0133I, which covers the four-pot turbo hybrid version of the 250-series Land Cruiser Prado.
Production dates range from July 15, 2024, through October 6, 2026. So yeah, the problem has only recently been contained in vehicle production. Toyota Motor (China) Investment handles the Lexus side of the biz. Its recall, which is listed as S2026M0134I, includes GX 550h vehicles manufactured in Japan between February 28, 2024, and October 1, 2026.
While they may be handled as separate campaigns, the problem is shared. Furthermore, the manufacturing windows also overlap considerably. Regarding the remedy, service technicians first have to inspect the quick-connect fittings. If no abnormalities are found, Toyota and Lexus techs are to install an additional fixing cover designed to prevent a separation.
Photo: Toyota Vehicles that seem a bit off, meanwhile, will receive a brand-new fuel line assembly and the fixing cover as well. Naturally, these remedies come at no charge to affected customers in the People's Republic of China. The SAMR filing also reveals that customers will be contacted through registered mail and other channels. Alternatively, customers may contact Toyota and Lexus by phone.
Additional details are available via the State Administration for Market Regulation Recall Center or on the SAMRDPRC WeChat account. Last but certainly not least, neither brand has announced a deadline for completing the inspections. The campaigns, however, take effect immediately.
The China-built model is advertised with 326 ponies at full throttle. Equipped with a NiMH battery, an eight-speed automatic tranny, and full-time AWD with a locking center differential, the Prado for the PRC outputs 630 Newton-meters (465 pound-feet) of torque. Said components and figures are shared with the GX 550h, which is understandably pricier due to its badge and more generous standard kit.
778,000 yuan is the starting price of the Pioneer grade, whereas 899,800 yuan gets you the Lingfeng ULTRA trim level. At current exchange rates, those prices can be converted to 116,320 and 134,530 dollars.

Want To Drift an AMG? This Florida Motor Club Has Your Back, and You Can Bring the Family, Too
18 photos
Photo: P1 Motor Club
There is a private motor club in Florida where Mercedes-AMG models are now standard-issue track cars for resident members. That arrangement is the result of a new partnership between P1 Motor Club and Mercedes-Benz USA, which officially makes Mercedes-Benz and its AMG performance division the Official Automotive Partner of the 650-acre (263-hectare) motorsports facility located in Port St. Lucie.
The German automaker will establish a permanent vehicle and operational presence across the Florida property. Through the deal, Mercedes-Benz USA will supply the venue with an ongoing fleet of Mercedes-Benz and Mercedes-AMG vehicles spanning high-performance sports cars, standard luxury passenger models, off-road utilities, and commercial Sprinter vans to support daily operations across the site.
P1 Motor Club plans to deploy this manufacturer-backed fleet across several internal departments, covering track driving sessions, guest hospitality, member transportation, and day-to-day logistics. Within that supplied lineup, Mercedes-AMG models are slated to serve as the primary street-car rentals for club-managed members, visiting guests, and corporate driving groups booking track time at the motorsports complex.
Beyond basic track rentals, the supplied vehicles will be integrated directly into P1 Motor Club's internal instructional programs. The fleet will support the facility's high-performance driving and racing schools, off-road and rally courses, and general driver coaching. This allows members and guests to use factory-supplied cars across the club's various asphalt and loose-surface training areas instead of relying solely on personal vehicles.
Photo: P1 Motor Club In addition to supplying cars, the agreement designates the Port St. Lucie venue as a primary United States operating base for select AMG Experience driving programs and brand activations. In other words, when a new Mercedes or AMG model breaks ground (from the most savage hypercars and supercars to the humblest daily drivers), the P1 Motor Club members will get their hands on them before regular customers.
This brings the automaker's complete factory driving academy—consisting of the Performance, Advanced, Pro, Pro+, Drift, and Drift+ training courses—directly to the Florida venue for both novice drivers and experienced track enthusiasts.
These factory-run courses will operate alongside P1 Motor Club's existing in-house curriculum, which already includes racing schools, drift instruction, rallycross sessions, karting programs, and private coaching. Mercedes-Benz USA also plans to set up dedicated AMG-branded facilities on the campus and use the property's track infrastructure to host recurring customer drive events and official brand activations throughout the year for invited drivers.
Photo: P1 Motor Club Aurora Straus, a Founding Partner of P1 Motor Club and a professional racing driver who competes in Mercedes-AMG machinery on race weekends, said the partnership is designed to integrate the automaker into the daily routine of the club. According to Straus, placing the brand in the garages, classrooms, and racetracks gives members and their families direct access to the company's vehicles and instruction.
Located on Florida's Treasure Coast about 45 minutes north of Palm Beach, P1 Motor Club contains more than 9 miles (14.5 kilometers) of private tracks, including a 4.5-mile (7.2-kilometer) FIA Grade 2 circuit, a 3-mile (4.8-kilometer) secondary course, and karting, drift, and rally layouts. The invitation-only club also features garage townhomes, residences, and a clubhouse for Charter License holders.
